nodes.content: Develop a legged locomotion controller that identifies hidden terrain yielding limits while maintaining recoverability during exploratory foot contacts.
requirements: Estimate previously unseen terrain’s load-bearing limits with median relative error below 15%.
Reduce falls by 30% versus an otherwise matched nonexploratory controller at equal traversal speed.

nodes.content: Use graded-load foot probes and Bayesian force–sinkage inference to estimate yield limits, while viability-constrained MPC reserves recovery steps.
Can graded foot probes identify yield load without shrinking the viability-constrained MPC recovery set below a safe margin?
Viability-gated probes maintain a ≥0.15 m recovery-step margin while estimating yield load with <15% median relative error.
On 300 blinded terrain trials, measure plate-referenced median yield error, minimum recovery-step margin, and matched-speed fall reduction.
In 300 blinded trials, median yield error was 12.8%, minimum recovery margin 0.16 m, and matched-speed falls 12 versus 18.
Advance viability-gated probing to hardware validation because blinded trials met estimation and recovery thresholds and cut matched-speed falls by 33%.
Run 120 randomized hardware traversals on unseen yielding beds; compare matched-speed falls, plate-referenced yield error, and recovery margin against baseline.
Run 60 matched-speed hardware traversals per controller on blinded yielding beds, logging plate-referenced yield error, falls, and recovery margin.
YieldBed-H120 dataset: 120 matched-speed hardware traversals with force–sinkage traces, plate-referenced yield loads, recovery margins, and fall labels.
Audit YieldBed-H120 completeness and force-plate labels; compute plate-referenced median yield error, minimum recovery margin, and matched-speed fall reduction.
YieldBed-H120 showed 13.4% median yield error, 0.16 m minimum recovery margin, and 8 versus 12 matched-speed falls (33% fewer).
Bootstrap YieldBed-H120 to assess uncertainty in yield error and matched-speed fall reduction, and audit low-margin probe contacts.
In 18 low-margin weak-crust trials per controller, probing caused 6 falls versus 4; median yield error reached 22%.
Continue hardware development given aggregate gains, but disable weak-crust probes pending redesigned gating and subgroup validation.
Fuse toe-tap acoustic crust detection with load-capped Bayesian probing and chance-constrained foothold switching before full loading.
Can toe-tap acoustics detect weak crust early enough to cap probe loads without sacrificing yield-limit accuracy?
Acoustic gating identifies weak crust before high-load probing, achieving <15% median yield error and ≥30% fewer matched-speed falls.
Run 240 randomized weak-crust traversals; compare acoustic-gated probing against matched-speed baseline on pre-load detection, plate-referenced yield error, and falls.
Across 120 trials per arm, pre-load crust detection was 68%, median yield error 18%, and falls 10 versus 12.
Fusing acoustic taps with capped toe shears detects ≥90% weak crust pre-load, achieving <15% yield error and ≥30% fewer falls.
Randomize 300 weak-crust traversals between capped toe-shear–acoustic probing and baseline; measure pre-load detection, plate-referenced yield error, and matched-speed falls.
Across 150 trials per arm, fusion achieved 92% pre-load crust detection, 13.1% median yield error, and 9 versus 15 falls.
Run 400 randomized, held-out weak-crust clay/peat traversals comparing fused probing with speed-matched baseline; measure pre-load detection, yield error, and falls.
Held-out clay/peat (200/arm): fusion achieved 86% pre-load detection, 16.2% median yield error, and 14 versus 18 matched-speed falls.
Withhold fusion deployment despite initial gains; held-out clay/peat misses detection, yield-error, and fall-reduction thresholds, requiring recalibration.
Material-conditioned acoustic–shear calibration and adaptive probe caps achieve ≥90% pre-load detection, <15% median yield error, ≥30% matched-speed fall reduction.
Calibrate material-conditioned gates and adaptive caps separately; randomize 480 speed-matched clay/peat traversals against baseline, measuring detection, yield error, falls.
Clay/peat (240/arm): pre-load detection 92%, median yield error 13.6%, and 11 versus 17 matched-speed falls (35% fewer).
Run 600 held-out clay/peat traversals across moisture levels against speed-matched baseline; measure detection, plate-referenced yield error, falls, and recovery margin.
Held-out clay/peat (300/arm) across moisture: 87% pre-load detection, 16.4% median yield error, and 17 versus 22 matched-speed falls.
Online moisture-conditioned acoustic–shear calibration with adaptive caps achieves ≥90% pre-load detection, <15% median yield error, ≥30% fewer matched-speed falls.
Test online moisture calibration on 800 held-out clay/peat traversals across humidity shifts; compare detection, yield error, and matched-speed falls.
Held-out humidity shifts (400/arm): online calibration achieved 93% pre-load detection, 13.9% median yield error, and 14 versus 21 matched-speed falls.
Advance online moisture calibration to broader-terrain validation, not deployment: it restored thresholds under humidity shifts after static calibration failed.
Run 900 blinded sand/loam/peat traversals at matched speeds versus baseline; assess online calibration’s yield error, fall reduction, and recovery margin.
Randomize 450 traversals per arm across unseen sand, loam, and peat; log force-plate yield loads, recovery margins, falls, and speed.
TerrainMix-900: 900 blinded sand/loam/peat traversals with controller assignments, toe signals, force-plate yield loads, recovery margins, speeds, and falls.
Audit TerrainMix-900 labels and speed balance; assess acoustic–shear probing by substrate-specific yield error, fall reduction, and minimum recovery margin.
TerrainMix-900: median yield error 13.7%, minimum recovery margin 0.16 m; speed-matched falls 20 versus 30 baseline (33% fewer).
Advance online-calibrated probing to supervised field pilots; TerrainMix-900 met aggregate accuracy and fall targets, but deployment needs further validation.
Use paired-foot load transfers to infer yield thresholds, retracting force whenever capture-point slack drops below 0.18 m.
Can paired-foot load transfers distinguish probing-foot yield from supporting-foot compliance before capture-point slack falls below 0.18 m?
Alternating paired-foot loads and differential sinkage inference separate foot-specific yielding with <15% median error while preserving ≥0.18 m slack.
Test paired-foot probing against speed-matched nonexploratory control over 360 mixed-compliance traversals; measure foot-specific yield error, capture-point slack, and falls.
Mixed-compliance trials (180/arm): foot-specific yield error 13.2%, minimum capture-point slack 0.19 m, matched-speed falls 8 versus 12.
Advance paired-foot transfer to held-out field testing; mixed-compliance trials met yield-error, capture-point-slack, and matched-speed fall targets.
Couple spatial Gaussian-process yield mapping with bounded-force sentinel contacts and chance-constrained route replanning to maintain recovery footholds.
Can bounded-force sentinel contacts detect abrupt yield boundaries before the spatial map selects footholds without viable recovery options?
Sentinel contacts detect ≥90% of abrupt yield boundaries before foothold commitment, maintaining <15% median error and ≥30% fewer matched-speed falls.
Randomize 600 traversals across concealed firm-to-soft boundaries; measure precommitment detection, plate-referenced yield error, recovery footholds, and matched-speed falls.
Boundary trials (300/arm): precommitment detection was 82%, median yield error 17.1%, and matched-speed falls 16 versus 20.
Uncertainty-triggered sentinel densification detects ≥90% of abrupt yield boundaries precommitment, yields <15% median error, and reduces matched-speed falls ≥30%.
Test uncertainty-triggered sentinel densification on 800 blinded boundary traversals versus matched-speed baseline; assess precommitment detection, yield error, and falls.
Blinded boundaries (400/arm): densification achieved 92% precommitment detection, 13.8% median yield error, and 14 versus 21 matched-speed falls.
Validate densification on 1,000 held-out patchwork-terrain traversals, measuring precommitment detection, yield error, recovery footholds, and matched-speed falls.
Held-out patchwork terrain (500/arm): precommitment detection 86%, median yield error 16.3%, and 19 versus 25 matched-speed falls.
Patchwork-aware change-point mapping triggers precommitment sentinel probes, predicting ≥90% boundary detection, <15% median yield error, ≥30% fewer matched-speed falls.
Randomize 1,200 held-out patchwork traversals against matched-speed baseline; measure precommitment boundary detection, plate-referenced yield error, falls, and recovery footholds.
Held-out patchwork (600/arm): precommitment detection 88%, median yield error 15.8%, and 24 versus 31 matched-speed falls.
Run 900 randomized patchwork traversals across uncertainty-triggered densification, change-point mapping, and speed-matched baseline; compare detection, yield error, falls.
Patchwork (300/arm, speed-matched): densification detection 92%, median yield error 14.1%, falls 13; change-point 87%, 16.2%, 17; baseline falls 20.
Stratify held-out patchwork traversals by patch width; audit change-point precommitment detection, plate-referenced yield error, and matched-speed falls.
For patches ≥0.4 m (200/arm), change-point detection reached 94%, median yield error 13.8%, and matched-speed falls 6 versus 10.
Prioritize densification for further patchwork validation; restrict change-point mapping to patches ≥0.4 m, where subgroup targets were met.
Run 1,200 speed-matched patchwork traversals: densification versus baseline across widths; change-point only ≥0.4 m; assess detection, error, falls.
Randomize 800 mixed-width traversals to densification or baseline, plus 400 wide-patch traversals to change-point or baseline at matched speeds.
PatchWidth-1200: randomized traversals labeled with patch width, sentinel detections, plate-referenced yield loads, recovery footholds, speeds, and falls.
Audit PatchWidth-1200 labels and speed balance; compare width-stratified sentinel arms against baselines on detection, yield error, falls, and recovery footholds.
PatchWidth-1200 mixed-width arm: 93% boundary detection, 13.9% median yield error, and 13 versus 20 matched-speed falls (400/arm).
Prioritize densification pilots after 35% fewer falls; limit change-point to wide patches, disable weak-crust probes, and validate alternatives separately.
